components.note: 门 (door/gate) — 间 pictures light passing through an entryway.
日 (sun) — sunlight shining through a gap in a doorway gave 间 its meaning of a space 'in between,' as in 中间 (in the middle) or 时间 (time, the space between moments).
讠 (speech) — 谍 relates to secretly gathering and reporting information.
枼 (yè) gives a sound only distantly related to dié today, having drifted apart over time.
王 (jade, written without its dot) — 玩 originally meant to handle and admire a piece of jade, extending to 'to play, to have fun.'
元 (yuán) gives a sound distantly related to wán, having drifted apart over time.
八 (two hands) — holding something up.
目 (a container/tray) — held between the two hands, the image behind 具's meaning 'tool, utensil.'
A simplified form of 車, a pictograph of a two-wheeled cart seen from above — the wheels, axle, and frame are visible in the original shape — the source of 车's meaning 'cart, vehicle.'
A short stroke placed above a longer one — a simple graphic way to show 'up' or 'above,' contrasted with 下 (down), which flips the strokes.
木 (wood) — 机 originally referred to a wooden device or machine, such as a loom.
几 depicts a small table or stool — combined with 木 (wood), the character pictured a wooden machine or mechanism.
口 (a vessel), shown four times — a set of cooking vessels.
犬 (a dog) — guarding the vessels, the source of 器's meaning 'vessel, tool, instrument.'
A simple line drawing of a person's legs seen from the side, used to depict a human being.
氵 (water) — relates to 满's meaning 'full,' water filling to the brim.
㒼 (mán) gives a sound hint — 满 is pronounced mǎn, sharing the same base sound with a different tone.
足 depicts a leg (the upper shape) above a foot — a simple picture of the human leg and foot, giving 足 its meaning 'foot, to be sufficient.'
扌 (hand) — 打 relates to hitting or performing an action with the hand.
丁 (dīng) gives the sound — 打 is pronounced dǎ, a connection that has shifted in tone.
攵 (a striking hand) — 败 relates to being struck down or defeated.
贝 (bèi) gives a sound close to bài, sharing the same initial.
The oracle-bone form has been interpreted as a bird flying up toward the sky; the meaning later shifted entirely to represent negation, 'not.'
冂 (a simplified eye shape in 见's modern form) — emphasizes the act of seeing.
儿 (a person) — a person with an emphasized eye above gives 见 its meaning 'to see.'
石 (stone) — 确 originally meant firm and solid like stone, extending to 'true, accurate, indeed.'
角 (jiǎo) served as the phonetic base; its pronunciation has since drifted well away from què.
The oracle-bone form has been interpreted as a bird flying up toward the sky; the meaning later shifted entirely to represent negation, 'not.'
⺮ (bamboo) — 管 originally referred to a bamboo pipe or tube, later broadening to mean 'to manage' or 'to control.'
官 (guān) gives a hint of the sound — 管 is pronounced guǎn, a connection that has shifted only slightly in tone.
心 (heart/mind) — 怎's meaning 'how' relates to a mental inquiry, what's on one's mind.
乍 (zhà) served as the phonetic base; its pronunciation has since drifted well away from zěn.
木 (tree/wood) — 样 originally referred to a kind of tree, later broadening to mean 'kind, appearance, way.'
羊 (yáng) gives the sound — 样 is pronounced yàng, matching aside from tone.
亻 (person) — relates to 传's meaning 'to pass on, transmit,' something passed from person to person.
专 (zhuān) gives a sound hint — 传 is pronounced chuán, sharing the same rhyme though the initial consonant differs.
纟 (thread) — 统 relates to threads gathered into one continuous strand, extending to the idea of unifying or governing as one system.
充 (chōng) gives a hint of the sound — 统 is pronounced tǒng, a connection that has shifted somewhat.
氵 (water) — 浪 names movement on the surface of water, a wave.
良 (liáng) gives a rhyme close to làng, with a different initial and tone.
氵 (water) — 漫 describes water overflowing and spreading everywhere.
曼 (màn) gives the sound — an exact match with 漫.

meanings: variant of 重複|重复[chong2 fu4]

components.note: 千 (thousand) — 重 pictures a heavy burden carried a great distance.
里 (a unit of distance, like a mile) — carrying something a thousand 里 emphasizes how heavy and significant a burden it is, giving 重 its meaning 'heavy' or 'important.'
亻 (a person) — the one repeating the routine.
日 (day, sun) — going somewhere every day, a repeated routine giving 复 its meaning 'to repeat, return; again.'
口 (mouth) — ties to harmony as speaking together in accord
禾 (hé, grain) gives the sound — matches 和's pronunciation hé
平 depicts a balance scale drawn level and symmetrical — a simple picture of flatness and equality.
欠 (an open mouth, as in a sigh or gasp) — 欣 describes an open expression of joy, 'happy, delighted.'
斤 (jīn) shares the rhyme -in with xīn, and both belong to the same historical initial series (j/q/x) — only the specific initial and tone differ.
贝 (money) — 赏 describes giving money or valuables as a reward.
尚 (shàng) gives a sound very close to shǎng, sharing the initial and rhyme — only the tone differs.
A short stroke placed below a longer one — the mirror image of 上 (up), together forming a simple, opposite pair.
Originally depicted a wheat plant; this agricultural picture was borrowed early on to represent the unrelated verb 'to come.'
大 (a person, arms outstretched) — represents a human being.
一 (a line, here representing the sky) — drawn above a person, showing what is above them: the heavens, hence 'sky, day.'
气 (simplified from 氣) depicts rising wisps or vapor, like breath or steam drifting upward — a simple picture of air or gas.
A single horizontal stroke — the simplest possible way to represent the number one; some traditional interpretations link it to heaven or earth as the very first stroke of creation.
A single horizontal stroke — the simplest possible way to represent the number one; some traditional interpretations link it to heaven or earth as the very first stroke of creation.
心 (heart/mind) — 态 relates to one's inner state, manner, or attitude
太 (tài) gives the sound — 态 is also pronounced tài, an exact match
广 (a building or shelter) — 度 pictures people gathering indoors.
廿 (twenty) — a group of people meeting to measure or deliberate gave 度 its meaning of a 'degree' or 'measure,' as in temperature or angles.
尢 (lame/crooked leg) — 尴 groups awkwardness with this radical, suggesting an unsteady, uncomfortable position.
监 (jiān) gives a sound close to gān, sharing the same rhyme.
尢 (lame/crooked leg) — like 尴, 尬 groups awkwardness with this radical of an unsteady stance.
介 (jiè) gives a sound distantly related to gà, having drifted apart over time.
亻 (person) plus 尔 (an old second-person pronoun) — combines to form 你, the modern word for 'you.'
女 (woman) — represents a mother.
子 (child/son) — a mother together with her child was seen as an image of goodness, giving 好 its meaning 'good.'
又 (a hand) — reaching out to try to catch something.
隹 (a bird) — catching a bird by hand is hard, giving 难 its meaning 'difficult.'
又 (a hand) — reaching out for support.
十 (a branch) — held in the hand, the image of support giving 支 its meaning 'to support, prop up; branch.'
覀 here depicts rising flames.
示 (altar) — burning paper offerings over an altar, a traditional practice, gave 票 its meaning of a paper note, later 'ticket, banknote.'
女 (woman) — represents a mother.
子 (child/son) — a mother together with her child was seen as an image of goodness, giving 好 its meaning 'good.'
王 (jade, written without its dot) — 玩 originally meant to handle and admire a piece of jade, extending to 'to play, to have fun.'
元 (yuán) gives a sound distantly related to wán, having drifted apart over time.
日 (sun) — represents the sun.
十 depicts the first rays of sunlight appearing low on the horizon — together with 日 (sun) giving 早 its meaning 'early, morning.'
食 (food) — 餐 relates directly to eating and meals.
A picture of a nose; because people in ancient China would point to their own nose when referring to themselves, the character came to mean 'self.'
A short stroke placed above a longer one — a simple graphic way to show 'up' or 'above,' contrasted with 下 (down), which flips the strokes.
冖 (a covering/roof) — represents the building or schoolhouse where learning happens.
子 (child) — 学 depicts children gathered to study.
⺍ is a small graphic element at the top of the character; its original pictorial meaning, if any, has been lost over time.
攵 (a hand with an implement, action) — relates to 放's meaning 'to let go, release, put.'
方 (fāng) gives the sound — 放 is pronounced fàng, a close match sharing the same rhyme.
土 (earth/soil) — 在 originally related to standing on the ground
才 (cái) gives the sound — 在 is pronounced zài, a close match
屮 (a young shoot) growing up out of 土 (earth/soil) — a picture of new life emerging from the ground.
牛 (ox/cattle) — cattle were among the earliest and most valuable kinds of property, connecting 物 to the general idea of 'object' or 'thing.'
勿 (wù) gives the sound — 物 is also pronounced wù, an exact match.
王 (a variant form of 玉, meaning jade) — 理 originally referred to the natural grain or pattern in jade, later extending to 'reason, logic, to manage.'
里 (lǐ) gives the sound — 理 is also pronounced lǐ, an exact match.
讠 (speech) — 论 relates to discussing or explaining something with words.
仑 (logical order, arrangement) — combined with speech, 论 came to mean 'to discuss' or 'a theory,' explaining ideas in an orderly way.
A drawing of a ridged, pointed animal horn.
广 (a building or shelter) — 度 pictures people gathering indoors.
廿 (twenty) — a group of people meeting to measure or deliberate gave 度 its meaning of a 'degree' or 'measure,' as in temperature or angles.
干 (originally a person) shown carrying a heavy load of grain on their back — since harvests came once a year, the character came to mean 'year.'
纟 (thread) — 纪 relates to organizing threads in order, extended to mean 'record, era'
己 (jǐ) gives a sound close to 纪's reading jì
弓 (a bow) — the curved frame.
丨 (a straight line), shown twice — arrows or a bowstring pulled tight across it; the character is mostly used today in transliteration.
A stylized drawing of orchid blossoms and leaves growing up from the ground.
十 (here representing a weapon or armor) — 克 pictures overcoming an opponent.
兄 (a person, here representing a formidable figure) — overcoming a strong opponent gave 克 its meaning 'to overcome' or 'to be able to.'
见 (to see) — the act of looking.
又 (again, or a hand) — looking closely or repeatedly, giving 观 its meaning 'to observe, view.'
宀 (roof) — 察 relates to careful observation
祭 (jì) gives a loose sound connection to 察's reading chá
耂 (a person bent with age, with long hair) — depicts an elderly figure.
匕 (here representing a cane or walking stick) — combined with the bent figure above, 老 pictures an old person leaning on a cane.
鼠 pictures a mouse in profile, with paws on one side and a long tail trailing on the other, giving the character its meaning 'mouse, rat.'
田 (field) — represents farmland.
力 (strength/effort) — someone strong enough to work the fields gave 男 its meaning 'male, man.'
又 (hand), shown twice and joined together — two hands clasped in friendship gave 友 its meaning 'friend.'
扌 (hand) — 掉 relates to dropping something from the hand.
卓 (zhuó) reflects an older phonetic connection that has faded in the modern pronunciation diào.
口 (mouth) — 吃 relates to eating, done with the mouth
乞 (qǐ) gives a sound close to 吃's reading chī
忄 (heart) — 惊 relates to an emotional reaction of shock or fright
京 (jīng) gives the sound — an exact match with 惊's reading jīng
A drawing of a person standing with arms and legs spread wide — used to represent the idea of something being 'big' or 'great.'
木 (wood) — buildings were traditionally framed with wood.
娄 (lóu) gives the sound — an exact match with 楼.
力 (strength/force) — 动 relates to movement produced by exertion or force.
冏 (bright, a window admitting light) — appears in 商's ancient form, though its exact link to 'commerce, to discuss' is unclear today.
章 — a graphic element whose original contribution to the character's meaning has been lost over time.
广 (shelter/building) — 店 names a building used for business.
占 (zhàn) gives a sound distantly related to diàn, having drifted apart over time.
女 depicts a kneeling woman.
支 depicts a hand holding a branch, suggesting work or a trade — paired with 女, it originally marked a woman working as an entertainer, giving 妓 its meaning 'prostitute.'
女 depicts a kneeling figure with arms crossed, a traditional posture — a simple picture of a woman.
The oracle-bone form has been interpreted as a bird flying up toward the sky; the meaning later shifted entirely to represent negation, 'not.'
斤 (an axe) — cutting through something.
米 (grain, in the simplified form; a bundle of thread in the traditional 斷) — the material being cut, giving 断 its meaning 'to break off, cut, sever.'
Originally a drawing of a bear, with 厶 as its head, ⺼ as its body, and 匕匕 as its claws; the picture was later borrowed to mean 'ability, to be able to.'
里 (a unit of distance, related to a village measure) — 量 relates to measuring quantity.
旦 (dàn) gives a hint of the sound — 量 is pronounced liàng, a connection that has shifted significantly over time.
灬 (fire) — 熟 describes food that has been cooked thoroughly over fire.
孰 (shú) gives the sound — an exact match with 熟's reading shú.
心 (mind) — 悉 describes coming to fully know or understand something in one's mind.
釆 (biàn) is only distantly related in sound to xī — the connection has drifted apart to the point of being barely recognizable.
八 here depicts something splitting apart or being divided.
厶 is an old form meaning 'private' or 'one's own' — 公 shows dividing up private property to share it fairly, giving rise to the meaning 'public' or 'fair.'
丶 (a dot) — represents the burning flame atop a lamp.
王 here depicts the base and stand of an oil lamp, not its usual meaning 'king' — the one who tends the flame became linked to 'master, lord, main.'
月 (yuè) here actually derives from 肉 (meat) — 有 originally depicted a hand holding meat, meaning 'to possess'; it also lends a loose phonetic connection to yǒu.
攵 (an action/to strike) — 效 relates to the result produced by an action
交 (jiāo) gives a sound close to 效's reading xiào
羊 (sheep; here representing feathers or ornaments on a headdress) — an elaborate decoration worn on the head.
大 (a person, arms outstretched) — a person wearing a decorated headdress was seen as beautiful, giving 美 its meaning 'beautiful.'
金 depicts a bell or metal casting mold, with dots representing droplets of molten metal — a picture linked to metal and, later, specifically gold.
夕 (evening/night) — the darkness that has fallen
亻 (a person) — someone moving under cover of night
日 (sun) — the sun is what disappears as evening falls
免 (to escape, avoid) — pictured as the sun slipping away, giving 晚 its sense of 'late, evening'
氵 (water) — relates to 清's meaning 'clear (water), pure.'
青 (qīng) gives the sound — 清 is also pronounced qīng, an exact match.
酉 (wine jar) — 醒 originally described sobering up from drink, extending to 'to wake up.'
星 (xīng) gives a sound close to xǐng, sharing the same syllable body and differing mainly in tone.
